body.estimand_functional: \(C_n^{\mathrm{proj}}(\alpha)=\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{j\in\mathcal J}I_{j,n}(\alpha))\) is the feasible simultaneous projected confidence set. On the unrestricted-effect full Gaussian face space, \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha}^{G}(H,\Omega)=+\infty\). The finite repaired weak-separation benchmark is the score-only value \(\mathfrak R_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{sc}}(H,B,\Gamma)\), which observes \(b\) exactly and bounds only its spread.

sampling_model.design: There are fixed finite treated groups and prespecified donor stacks. Each donor stack has known comparison-group weights, and its score is the treated-minus-donor contrast in the prespecified baseline levels, pre-period slopes, and case-mix summaries contained in \(G_{ri}\). Exact population equality, not ranked sample proximity, defines a close donor.
sampling_model.units: At each \(n\), observations are independent within and across the fixed primitive groups under the product law \(\mathbb P_n=\bigotimes_{r\in\mathcal R}P_{r,n}^{\otimes n_r}\), with every limiting group fraction bounded away from zero. Shared treated groups and reused controls induce non-diagonal score covariance and are retained in \(\Gamma\).
sampling_model.treatment: Treatment is a fixed realized group-level history. Consistency identifies observed post outcomes with the corresponding potential outcomes. Causal transport additionally requires the nonempty exact-close condition and the additive untreated-change condition \(\mathbb E[Y_{ri}(0)-Y_{ri}^{\mathrm{pre}}\mid G_{ri}]=\kappa_n+\beta_n^{\top}G_{ri}\); these are substantive crux assumptions, not consequences of Gaussian approximation.
sampling_model.overlap: Every primitive group has a limiting sample fraction bounded away from zero. No treatment-propensity overlap condition is invoked, but the finite donor menu must contain at least one exact population-close label in every law under which causal coverage is claimed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Group means and within-group covariance matrices are estimated directly, and the known contrast matrix propagates covariance from shared treated groups and reused controls. Spectral clipping totalizes the feasible panel inversions. In the corrected local decision experiment, only the root-sample-scaled score vector has Gaussian noise; the unscaled donor-effect vector is observed exactly, and its spread is bounded by \(B\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Argmax-winner inference motivates separating honest projection from oracle behavior, but its selection rule and estimand differ from the exact-zero donor-face model.
Expected-measure confidence-set duality is only a template unless domination, product measurability, and a reduction from fixed-measure loss to diameter are proved for donor faces.
Simultaneous inference motivates universal post-selection validity, not minimax optimality of the maximum-critical donor hull.
Weak-identification subsequence methods motivate uniformity analysis but do not establish score-only Le Cam risk transfer for donor faces.
Conditional Gaussian inference motivates identification-robust calibration but does not supply the corrected score-only experiment equivalence.
Few-treated-group inference with many controls is distinct from inference driven by many micro observations within a fixed finite set of labels.
Time-series synthetic-control inference is distinct from exact-score donor-label uncertainty in fixed-label micro-panels.
Global asymptotic equivalence requires substantially stronger domination, smoothness, positivity, compactness, and likelihood-process control than the panel moment assumptions provide.

body.tldr: A finite menu of prespecified donor stacks creates nonregular inference when validity is defined by an exact zero of a noisy baseline score. The panel confidence procedures remain causal only under the explicit nonempty exact-close condition and the shared-slope additive untreated-change condition; zero score alone does not imply target coherence in the abstract Gaussian limit. The unrestricted-effect full Gaussian frontier is infinite. The finite repair mandated by this obstruction observes the unscaled donor effects exactly, keeps Gaussian noise only in the root-sample-scaled scores, and bounds their spread by \(B\) while leaving absolute location unrestricted. Its two-state value is exactly \(\Delta[\Phi(z_{1-\alpha}-\rho)-\alpha]_+\), with a zero-diameter elbow at \(\rho=2z_{1-\alpha}\); a simultaneous score-screen hull gives the general finite bound \(B\), while the exact general-face constant remains open. None of these conditional results validates the historical CMS comparison-state estimates.

project_justification.gap: Existing few-treated panel and synthetic-control methods do not solve honest expected-diameter inference when a valid donor label is defined by an exact zero score and several labels may lie on the same face. Generic post-selection results also do not determine the minimax constant for this discontinuous target map.
project_justification.niche: The CMS comparison-state workflow has finitely many candidate labels, many beneficiaries within each state, unequal sample sizes, reused controls, and uncertainty about exact transport. A causal conclusion requires an exact population equality plus a model connecting the score to untreated changes. Ranked empirical balance supplies neither, and the abstract implication from zero scores to a common effect is an additional restriction rather than an algebraic fact.
project_justification.fill: The project proves exact-close transport under the explicit shared-slope untreated-change model, gives uniformly honest simultaneous and pilot-adaptive procedures with fixed-separation oracle behavior, proves that the originally frozen full Gaussian frontier is infinite when effect spread is unrestricted, and supplies the bounded-spread score-only repair. The repaired experiment has an exact two-state Mahalanobis minimax formula, a general embedded-pair lower bound, and a simultaneous-screen upper bound \(B\); only the exact general finite-face constant and a fully justified finite-sample-to-score-only risk transfer remain open.

body.related_work: The reviewed RTI material describes the CMS comparison-state workflow through ranked baseline distance, retained comparison states, claims-driven substitutions, and person-level weighting; it does not document ex ante algebraic calibration to known population totals for every score component. Hence the workflow is a motivating and falsifiable use case, not evidence that the paper's exact-close assumptions held historically. Conley and Taber and Ferman and Pinto obtain reference variation from many control groups, unlike the many-within-group, fixed-label regime here. Chernozhukov, Wuthrich, and Zhu study time-series synthetic-control inference rather than exact donor-face uncertainty. Berk et al. motivate simultaneous protection but do not establish minimaxity of the maximum-critical hull. Andrews, Kitagawa, and McCloskey study argmax-winner selection; the present exact-zero-face model is not their argmax-selection model, and neither parameter class contains the other without changing both the selection rule and the estimand. Their work motivates the separate pilot-adaptive oracle construction only. Evans, Hansen, and Stark supply an acceptance-region expected-measure template, but their duality is not used as a theorem here because domination, product measurability, and the reduction from fixed sigma-finite expected measure to expected diameter have not been proved. Andrews and Cheng, Andrews and Mikusheva, and Nussbaum motivate weak-limit and experiment-comparison questions but do not remove the effect-coordinate scaling obstruction or establish the required score-only risk transfer.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The unrestricted-effect full Gaussian benchmark has minimax expected diameter \(+\infty\), so no finite general program can attain it. The repaired score-only bounded-spread experiment has an exact two-state value and the finite general bound \(0\leq\mathfrak R_{\alpha}^{\mathrm{sc}}(H,B,\Gamma)\leq B\), including shared-control covariance and multiple-zero faces, but its exact general-\(J\) constant is not derived. Evans--Hansen--Stark duality remains only a template because the necessary domination, joint measurability, and expected-measure-to-diameter reduction are absent. Likewise, finite-sample transfer is claimed only after a future proof of two-sided uniform deficiency and uniform integrability for the score-only loss; the refuted fixed-noise effect-coordinate target is excluded. The accepted pilot-adaptive construction and its oracle-equivalence statement are unchanged.
body.honest_scope: Uniform causal coverage and fixed-separation oracle conclusions apply only to the triangular-array panel class satisfying consistency, stable group fractions, moment and covariance regularity, a nonempty exact close set, and the shared-slope additive untreated-change condition. In the abstract Gaussian face problems, equality of the \(b_j\) values at simultaneous zero-score labels is separately imposed and is not implied by \(h_j=0\). The original unrestricted-effect full Gaussian frontier is infinite. Finite weak-separation risk statements concern the corrected score-only experiment with exactly observed \(b\), positive definite \(\Gamma\), and spread at most \(B\); the exact theorem covers any two embedded faces and the simultaneous screen covers general finite faces, but exact general-face minimaxity and Le Cam risk transfer are not claimed. No reviewed source establishes the exact calibration assumptions for the historical CMS estimates.
body.interpretation: The infinite full Gaussian frontier is an ill-posedness diagnosis, not a failure of simultaneous panel coverage: with unrestricted \(b\), nearly indistinguishable score faces can select effects separated by arbitrarily large \(\Delta\). The bounded score-only experiment isolates the economically relevant weak-separation cost after ordinary post-mean noise has vanished. Exact two-face adaptation is governed by Mahalanobis score separation, while a covariance-aware simultaneous screen remains valid on multiple-zero faces. For the CMS workflow, the operational implication is to prespecify and audit exact calibration and untreated-trend transport; good ranked balance cannot be substituted for either condition.
